record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices. It contains some apparent OCR or typesetting artifacts, but the reported experimental tables and text are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains residual networks from random initialization and reports outcomes relevant to initialization and depth, but reports test accuracy rather than training classification error. Its initialization comparisons are a conceptual test of V4 and V3, not the exact measure specified in those versions.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own training results and initial signal-correlation measurement. Results cited from other work, and accuracy curves only described without numeric values, are not separate rows. Test accuracy does not establish whether the networks reached near-zero training error.
record.test_reason: The study develops and evaluates initialization for residual ReLU networks. V4 specifies learning speed and trainable depth in plain networks; the study's residual-network speed comparison does not test that version. Its final test accuracies and initial input correlations also do not establish training-error, speed, or depth effects in the systems specified by the other versions. No plain-versus-residual depth comparison or controlled BN training-speed comparison is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they claim exact initial dynamical isometry for residual ReLU networks, balanced residual and skip contributions, and stable, faster training, with competitive or often better benchmark performance. Their broad performance summaries need qualification: Table 1 favors Fixup over R ISOTTO for every Type B entry, and Table 2 favors He initialization for CIFAR100 Type C.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a distinct looks-linear orthogonal initialization for residual and skip branches, with SGD and benchmark image datasets; compares with Fixup, SkipInit, and He initializations. It does not report the claim's training-error measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes depend on dataset, block type (B/C), batch normalization, initialization, and the placement of a single BN layer. The text reports that R ISOTTO allows stable training across the tested single-BN placements, while standard initializations fail in some placements; exact values are figure-only.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 1 and 2 report final test accuracy for residual networks under different initializations. Results depend on block type, dataset, and BN; R ISOTTO exceeds Fixup for Type C without BN but falls below Fixup for every Type B entry.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization affects residual-network generalization performance, with advantages depending on architecture, dataset, and normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1b reports preserved initial input correlations with R ISOTTO; Section 2 derives norm preservation and dynamical isometry for its structured residual blocks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured orthogonal initialization can preserve initial signal geometry in residual ReLU networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3 and Figure 3 report faster attainment of good test accuracy for R ISOTTO than Fixup in ResNet101 (C) on CIFAR100, with similar final performance. Appendix A.4 specifies the same learning rate, 0.005, for these initializations. This comparison is already declared in rows_left_out.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: R ISOTTO can accelerate learning in deep residual ReLU networks relative to Fixup.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 2 and 5 report stable learning with R ISOTTO across single-BN placements, while standard initializations fail in some placements. These comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization affects residual-network training stability when normalization is sparse.

record.problems: The paper reports test accuracy rather than training classification error, limiting direct evidence for the claim. Main numeric comparisons use 3 runs. Some comparisons are only described in plots without numeric values. The authors report that Fixup and SkipInit can be susceptible to bad random seeds and failed runs; no failed-run counts are given.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numeric rows for accuracy curves in Figures 2–5, ResNet101 training speed in Figure 3, or NF ResNet comparisons in Figure 4: the text gives qualitative descriptions without numeric values. These figures compare outcomes relevant to initialization but don't supply reconstructable exact values.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including random or corrupted labels, and its dependence on size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation in plain networks, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated plain-tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Initialization-dependent learning speed and trainable depth in plain networks, equal-variance orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh comparisons, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional training.
Training above initial stability limits, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Controlled comparisons of accuracy-gain speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without BN, including whether Fixup matches BN training speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Reject the extracted V3 verdict: R1 contains neither a depth comparison nor a shortcut intervention. The corrected Table 1 values also invalidate several extracted performance directions. Differences between final test accuracies should not be converted into observed, partial, or reversed states for training-speed claims.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, label corruption, model size comparisons, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth-dependent training error and shortcut effects on training error are not measured; the paper reports test accuracy for selected depths.

The paper tests initialization choices in residual networks, but does not compare orthogonal versus Gaussian weights of equal variance in very deep plain tanh networks, nor train plain convolutional networks at 10,000 layers.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and loss divergence.
Whether batch normalization speeds accuracy gains or tolerates higher learning rates is not tested as a claim; BN is held as a condition in initialization comparisons.
